- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then overshoot, particularly after sharp upward spikes in the history.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — overestimates after recent high prices, then underestimates as prices correct downward.
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in the middle to late horizon.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting it fails to capture late-stage momentum or policy-driven corrections.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then gradually adjust — but often adjust too late or too much.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts rise sharply when history shows recent peaks, then fail to correct downward.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days, leading to underprediction of price spikes or corrections.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” sharp price drops, underestimating the magnitude of corrections.
- Model fails to account for policy or regulatory changes that cause sudden price shifts — especially in the last 5–10 days.
